articles.description:
In most small companies in Dubai, Riyadh or Doha, a purchase request travels like this: someone sends a photo of a quotation on WhatsApp, the manager replies "ok" two days later, finance asks "who approved this?" at month end, and nobody can find the message.
None of that is a software problem at first. It's a missing record. There is no single place that says what was requested, who approved it, when, and for how much. An approval workflow app is just that record, plus a few rules about who has to say yes.
This article walks through building one for a typical 20–80 person Gulf company: a trading firm, a clinic group, a real estate office, a training centre. It covers what to decide on paper first, then a step-by-step build in Mythex with the prompts you'd actually type, and the honest lim…
articles.title: How to build an approval workflow app for a small Gulf company: purchase requests, in Arabic and English

articles.author: Ivan Zdravkov
articles.description:
A 7B model is the honest ceiling for LoRA fine-tuning on a 16 GB consumer card, not because anything bigger throws an error, but because a 14B model silently spills into system memory and runs 50 times slower without ever reporting a failure.
Key takeaways
7B is the real ceiling on an RTX 5070 Ti at LoRA rank 16, sequence length 512, batch size 1: 11,897.9 MiB peak, well inside the card's 16,303 MiB.
14B completed without a raised exception in both tested conditions, but peak VRAM read 22,189.8 MiB (136% of the card) and 17,470.9 MiB (107%) - both over the physical limit, through Windows' silent system-memory fallback.
The cost of that fallback is severe: 21.7 seconds per training step at 14B against 0.4 seconds at 7B, roughly 51 times slower, with no error message anywhere.
Gradient check…
articles.title: LoRA on a 16 GB card: what fits and what does not

articles.author: Zhuang Hua
articles.description:
Agencies get asked "is our site accessible?" all the time. Most answers are either vague ("we follow WCAG") or a five-figure manual audit.
I built something in between: A11yKeeper — paste a URL, it runs axe-core across that page plus up to 9 linked pages (~1 min), groups issues by severity, and gives a plain-English fix for each.
It says clearly that a clean scan ≠ accessible. Deque's 2021 data puts automated detection at ~57% of issues by volume; every report ends with what a human still has to check (keyboard, screen reader, content).
No overlay, nothing injected into your site.
3 free scans/day, no signup to see results.
Agencies can put their own name on a white-label PDF for clients.
On the W3C's deliberately broken demo site it found 353 issues across 10 pages.
I'm looking for 5 founding agencies to shape scheduled re-checks and read-only client links — 50% off for as long as they stay subscribed.
Would love feedback on false positives or confusing fix text: https://a11ykeeper.com
Independent developer. Not a compliance certificate — a triage list.
articles.title: I built a free WCAG 2.2 checker that's honest about what automated scans miss

articles.author: Ivan Zdravkov
articles.description:
A kill-gate is a threshold written down before an experiment runs: if the result crosses it, the idea dies. The writing down happens first, because after the numbers arrive, every threshold becomes negotiable. Last week two of my gates fired and one refused to answer, which taught me more than a success would have.
Key takeaways
A kill-gate names, in advance, the number at which I abandon my own hypothesis; the plan file is frozen before the first run and never rewritten afterwards.
Gates exist because results negotiate: search-time contamination alone can inflate agent benchmark scores by up to 4%, and LLM-judge scores now come with conformal prediction intervals because point values wobble.
Of the three verdicts a gate can return, "cannot be pronounced" is the most valuable one: it indic…
articles.title: Why I pre-register a kill-gate for every experiment

articles.description:
If you write code for a living, you have probably felt two things at once about AI coding assistants. They can save real time. And they can waste real time when you pick the wrong one or trust it too far.
The trick is not finding the tool with the longest feature list. It is finding the one that fits the way you actually work, in your editor, with your stack, under your team's rules. This guide covers what these tools do well, where they fall short, and a simple way to choose without spending a month on trials.
At its core, a coding assistant predicts the next chunk of code based on your file, your comments, and the surrounding project. In day to day work, that shows up in a few useful places.
First, it speeds up the boring parts. Boilerplate, standard API calls, test scaffolding, and repe…
articles.title: Best AI Coding Assistants and How a Developer Should Pick One

articles.author: Omais Ali
articles.description:
A push notification to your phone is the simplest way to know what an Expert Advisor is doing while you are away from the terminal. MQL5 has one function for it, SendNotification(), and most EAs call it directly wherever something interesting happens.
That works until the day something goes wrong. A disconnect, a loop of rejected orders or a burst of partial fills makes the EA call SendNotification() many times in a few seconds. The terminal has strict limits on this function, and if they are broken it can disable notifications for the program. So the one moment you most need the alert is the moment it stops arriving.
This tutorial builds a small notifier that respects the limits, skips duplicates and still logs everything.
The message can be at most 255 characters.
No more than 2 calls pe…
articles.title: Sending push notifications from an MQL5 EA without getting them switched off

articles.author: Bohdan Hordii
articles.description:
Executive Problem Statement


Industrial automation teams and robotics companies are burning thousands of dollars monthly hosting high-VRAM GPU cloud nodes just to visualize and infer physical environments in real time. Radiance fields and standard 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS) promised photorealistic digital twins, but in production, they hit a brutal wall: extreme memory overhead, alpha-blending rasterization bottlenecks, and severe overdraw.
When autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) or edge telemetry nodes require spatial awareness, streaming heavy Gaussian representations over cellular/Wi-Fi links causes latency spikes and dropped frames. Engineering leaders are forced to choose between blurry, low-resolution low-poly meshes or unaffordable AWS EC2 G5/P4 instances operating at edge boundarie…
articles.title: Why 2D Gaussian Splatting Bleeds GPU Budgets: Hexels for Real-Time 3D Twins

Newspaper scans can hold valuable information, but getting that information into usable text isn't always straightforward. OCR can misread characters, distort words, and turn a perfectly readable page into a messy block of text.
For Week 4, I built Late Edition, a Python prototype that explores how language models can help correct OCR text while keeping potentially risky changes in check.
The idea was to let a model suggest repairs without automatically trusting everything it produces.

articles.author: athena wang
articles.description:
Why another AI video site?


Short-form trends move faster than full product roadmaps. One week everyone is filming a party walk with a bread bite and a blank stare (BbY WOW / Dime Dime Baby). The next week it is pet duets, street freestyle, or a green-booth cypher.
As a maker, I did not want a new domain and a new checkout for every meme. I wanted one boutique hub where each trend is a preset effect template: clear photo rules, a recorded sample with sound, and a short path from upload → pay → download.
That hub is AirapVideoMagic.
AirapVideoMagic is an AI rap / party video studio built around photo-to-video. You bring one or two clear reference photos; the effect supplies the scene, movement, and performance style. Think reference-guided generation (image-to-video / R2V-style fidelity): …
